newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends up, labour unrest affects trading.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends up, labour unrest affects trading.

text.p: The won closed firmer against the dollar on Thursday but trading sentiment was cautious due to the labour unrest over passage of a new labour law, dealers said.
The won ended at 843.90 after opening the day at an intraday low of 844.50. It touched a high of 843.50.
"Some banks started selling dollars, expecting no further sharp rise of the U.S. unit in the near future," said one dealer.
The sentiment was also affected by talk that the 845 won level would be kept as long as the central bank remained ready to intervene in the interbank trading to slow the won's drop.
The nation's two labour union organisations on Thursday called nearly two million members to strike in protest at the ruling New Korea Party's passage of a new labour law.
Workers at major carmakers and shipyards went on strike on Thursday and other unions, including hospital and subway workers, have declared their intention to join them.
The market reopened on Thursday after being closed for trading on Christmas Day.
Dealers expected the won's base mid-rate to be set at 843.90 on Friday, compared with 844.70 on Thursday.
